# Add state-aware affordability filtering for storyline options

## Summary

Extend `getStorylineOptions` (or add a companion state-aware accessor) that filters out unaffordable options based on `cost` fields. Store the presented/available option list on `PendingEventChoice` so indexing and save/load remain stable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Affordability filter.** `getAffordableOptions(state, event)` returns options where `cost` is affordable (coins and/or reputation gates checked). Options with no cost are always included.
- **Pending choice stores presented list.** `PendingEventChoice` gains an optional `presentedOptions: StorylineOption[]` field populated at choice-draw time.
- **Filtering is stable.** The presented list is computed once at draw and does not change during the pending choice period.
- **Backwards compatible.** Events with no cost-gated options return the same list as before.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — `getAffordableOptions()`, update `createPendingStorylineChoice()` to populate `presentedOptions`.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Add `presentedOptions` to `PendingEventChoice`.

## Deliverables

- New/pure function `getAffordableOptions`.
- `createPendingStorylineChoice` populates `presentedOptions`.
- Unit tests for affordability filter.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed — deterministic filtering.

# Deduct cost and apply extra effects during storyline option resolution

## Summary

At resolution time (`resolveStorylineOption` / `resolveEventOption`), deduct the option's `cost` from the player's resources and apply any `extraEffect` independently of the `effectPolicy`. This is the core gameplay change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Cost deduction.** When an affordable option is selected, its `cost.coins` (if set) and `cost.reputation` (if set) are deducted from `state.resourceBank`.
- **Extra effect application.** Any `extraEffect` is applied after cost deduction, independently of `effectPolicy`. Both can coexist (e.g. accept + pay cost + apply extra).
- **Log messages.** Activity log reflects cost deduction and extra effects.
- **Loss checks.** If deduction drops coins or reputation to zero, normal loss checks fire.
- **Backwards compatible.** Options without `cost` or `extraEffect` behave identically to pre-change.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — `resolveStorylineOption` applies cost + extra effect.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` logging updated.

## Deliverables

- Updated `resolveStorylineOption` and `resolveEventOption`.
- Updated log messages.
- Unit tests for cost/extra effect application.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNXOXW007OTLE (affordability filtering).
- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed — straightforward resource mutation.

# Resolve conditional successors at option resolution time

## Summary

When resolving an option, evaluate `conditionalSuccessors` in order — the first matching rule wins. Fall back to the option's existing `successorId` when no conditions match. This enables branching based on game state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Conditional evaluation.** `conditionalSuccessors` are evaluated sequentially; the first rule whose `{ field, op, value }` matches current `state.resourceBank.{field}` determines the pushed card ID.
- **Fallback.** When no conditions match, the option's `successorId` is used.
- **All boundary cases tested.** Above/below threshold, equality boundary (`==`), and no-match fallback.
- **Successor-card push.** The matched successor is pushed via `pushChainCard` as before.
- **Backwards compatible.** Options without `conditionalSuccessors` push `successorId` as before.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — Update `resolveStorylineOption` to evaluate conditional successors.

## Deliverables

- Conditional successor evaluation logic.
- Unit tests for each boundary/fallback case.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNYFJT006PKLC (cost deduction and extra effects).
- MS-0MURNXOXW007OTLE (affordability filtering).
- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed — pure predicate evaluation.

# Update resolveEventOption to use the stored presented option list

## Summary

`resolveEventOption` in `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` currently indexes into `getStorylineOptions(event)` (the full list). Update it to use `pending.presentedOptions` (the affordability-filtered list) so the option index stored at draw time maps correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Index into presented list.** `resolveEventOption` resolves using `pending.presentedOptions[optionIndex]` instead of `getStorylineOptions(event)[optionIndex]`.
- **Fallback to full list.** When `presentedOptions` is null/empty, fall back to `getStorylineOptions(event)`.
- **Transcript stability.** The transcript records the chosen option label from the presented list.
- **Backwards compatible.** Legacy events without `presentedOptions` behave identically.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` uses `pending.presentedOptions`.

## Deliverables

- Updated `resolveEventOption`.
- Unit tests confirming index stability.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNXOXW007OTLE (affordability filtering).
- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed.

# Update AI policy to select only among presented/affordable options

## Summary

`decideEventChoice` in `MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` currently returns `'accept' | 'reject'` and reasons about `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta`. Generalise it to select from the presented option list, accounting for cost and extra-effect deltas when projecting outcomes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AI selects from presented options.** The AI considers only options in the presented list (already filtered by affordability).
- **Cost-aware projection.** When projecting outcomes, the AI accounts for `cost` and `extraEffect` in addition to `effectPolicy` effects.
- **Regression harness passes.** The Monte Carlo and regression harnesses run to completion without AI stalls or invalid selections.
- **Backwards compatible.** For legacy binary-choice events, AI behaviour is identical to before.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `decideEventChoice` generalised for multi-way affordability-aware selection.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolvePendingEventChoice` wiring updated.

## Deliverables

- Updated AI policy.
- Regression/Monte Carlo harness tests green.
- Unit tests for AI policy with cost-gated options.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURO0VB30076NSE (engine turn closing update).
- MS-0MURNYFJT006PKLC (cost deduction and extra effects).
- MS-0MURNZWHY003TMBC (conditional successor resolution).
- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed — deterministic scoring policy.

# Extend storyline validator and schema to cover cost, extraEffect, conditionalSuccessors

## Summary

Update the static validator (`src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`) and the JSON schema (`schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`) to understand and validate the new optional fields. Reject invalid data (negative costs, unknown fields/ops, dangling conditional successors).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Cost validation.** Reject negative or zero costs.
- **Condition validation.** Reject conditions with unknown `field` or `op`; reject non-numeric `value`.
- **Extra effect validation.** Reject negative extra effect values.
- **Conditional successor validation.** Reject dangling conditional successors.
- **Shipped content validates cleanly.** All shipped CSVs produce valid storylines.
- **Schema updated.** JSON schema accepts the new optional fields.
- **Doc-drift test passes.**

# Intake Brief — Identify different AI players (MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF)

> **Status: final — producer decisions incorporated (Q1=A, Q2=A, Q3=A).**
> Recorded in the Appendix below; the item advanced to `intake_complete`.

## Problem Statement

In competitive (human vs AI) Main Street games the AI seats are not visually
distinguishable from one another or, at a glance, from the human seat. The
activity log, the scoreboard and the placed-card street all identify seats only
by ad-hoc text (`P0`, `AI 1`, `AI 2`), and placed cards carry no owner
indicator at all. A player therefore cannot reliably tell which AI made a given
move or which street slots belong to which opponent. This work assigns each AI
seat a distinct, colour-blind-friendly colour and threads that colour through
the UI.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants to identify at a glance which AI opponent made
  a move in the log and which street cards belong to which seat.
- **Colour-blind player** — wants seat colours that remain distinguishable
  under common forms of colour-vision deficiency.
- **Future example-game authors / designers** — reuse a shared seat-colour
  palette/assignment contract rather than inventing per-game colours.

### User Stories

- As a player, when an AI takes an action I see a coloured `AI 1` / `AI 2`
  prefix in the activity log (and `You`/`Pl` for the human), so I can tell who
  acted without reading the whole line.
- As a player, every placed business/community-space card carries a border in
  its owner's colour, so I can see ownership on the street at a glance.
- As a colour-blind player, the seat colours remain mutually distinguishable
  and are never the sole carrier of meaning (the seat label text is always
  present alongside the colour).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Distinct, colour-blind-friendly seat colours (Q2 = A).** In competitive
   mode each seat (human + every AI) is assigned a distinct colour from a fixed
   colour-blind-safe palette (e.g. Okabe–Ito); the palette is shuffled per game
   with an injected RNG so the assignment is deterministic for a given seed and
   stable across save/load. Verified by unit tests on the pure assignment
   helper (palette membership, mutual distinctness, seeded determinism,
   insufficient-palette guard) and a state save/load round-trip test.
2. **Log identifies the acting seat by colour + label.** Activity-log entries
   attributable to a seat are prefixed with that seat's label (`You` for the
   human, `AI 1`, `AI 2`, …) rendered in the seat's colour, and the prefix
   remains legible against the existing gain/loss/neutral line colour. Verified
   by unit/renderer tests.
3. **Placed cards carry an owner-coloured border (Q3 = A).** Every placed
   business/community-space card on the street carries an outer border in its
   owner's colour, with human and AI seats visually distinct; the full-card
   upgrade border is removed and the upgrade indicator moves to the existing
   top-left level badge / corner accent so upgrade state stays legible.
   Verified by renderer tests plus a manual/browser check.
4. **Colour is consistent everywhere a seat is identified.** The scoreboard,
   active-seat indicator, log prefixes and card borders all derive their seat
   colour from the same lookup, so a seat has one colour throughout the UI.
   Verified by a shared palette/lookup module and tests.
5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries** (notably
   `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` and the new module's JSDoc).
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Single-player is unchanged** — with one seat (the human) there are no AI
  colours and no behavioural or visual regression.
- **Colour-blind friendly** — the palette must be a recognised
  colour-vision-deficiency-safe set (e.g. Okabe–Ito) and large enough for the
  maximum supported AI opponent count; colour must never be the sole carrier of
  meaning (seat labels always accompany it).
- **Deterministic and testable** — colour assignment must accept an injected
  RNG (seeded) so it is reproducible in tests and replay, and must be persisted
  in competitive state/save so it does not reshuffle on reload.
- **Presentation-only** — no change to game rules, economy, AI decisions or
  scoring.
- **Reuse existing seams** — pure helpers must stay Phaser-free for Node unit
  tests; rendering must reuse the existing street/HUD renderers.
- **UK English spelling** in code comments, docs and UI copy.

## Existing State

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `PlayerRecord` has `playerId`, `controller`,
  `aiStrategy`, `aiDifficulty`, `eliminated`; **no colour field**.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts` — labels seats `You` /
  `AI <n>`; `MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts` colours rows with hard-coded
  hex (`#aaffaa` active, `#ffcc44` human, `#88bbff` AI).
- `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` — `addLog(state, text, type)` colours entries by
  `LogEntryType` (`gain` / `loss` / `neutral` / `turn-header`); seat
  attribution is ad-hoc text such as `P${ownerId}` and `AI ${playerId}` at call
  sites (e.g. `MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`, `MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`,
  `MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`).
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts` — `getSeatLabel(ownerId)` returns
  `the player` / `AI <ownerId>`; the shared seat-label source.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — `drawBusinessSlot` renders placed
  cards; `applyUpgradeOverlays` draws `spec.upgradeBorder` from
  `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` (a full-card stroke). No owner indicator
  exists.
- `MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K` ("Competitive rendering: owner-coloured street,
  shared-market phase alternation, SFX") scoped owner-coloured street rendering
  but was **deferred on 2026-10-03 and closed `done` without implementation**;
  the current street renderer has no owner tinting/border.
- No colour-blind-friendly palette or seat-colour lookup exists anywhere in the
  repo.

## Desired Change

1. Add a pure seat-colour module: a colour-blind-friendly palette plus an
   assignment helper that takes the seat list (human + AI) and an injected RNG
   and returns a distinct colour per seat, with a guard when the palette is too
   small.
2. Persist the per-seat colour in competitive state (`PlayerRecord`) and
   round-trip it through save/load.
3. Thread the seat colour into: activity-log seat prefixes, the competitive
   scoreboard/active-seat indicator, and the placed-card border.
4. Make the owner colour the outer card border and move the upgrade indicator
   to the existing top-left level badge / corner accent, removing the full-card
   upgrade border (Q3 = A) so both ownership and upgrade level remain legible.
5. Document the palette and its usage.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetSeatColours.ts` — **new**: palette + pure assignment/lookup helper.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — add `colour` to `PlayerRecord`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — assign seat colours in `createCompetitiveState`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — round-trip the per-seat colour.
- `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` and log call sites — seat-prefixed, seat-coloured entries.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts` — seat label / colour lookup seam.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — owner-coloured placed-card border; reconcile `applyUpgradeOverlays`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts` / `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts` — use seat colours.
- `tests/main-street/seat-colours.test.ts` — **new**: palette/assignment/round-trip tests.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — document the seat palette and usage.

## Related Work

- **Potentially related work items:**
  - `MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K` — *Competitive rendering: owner-coloured street,
    shared-market phase alternation, SFX* — deferred/closed without
    implementation; **superseded for the owner-colour scope by this item
    (Q1 = A)**; its phase-alternation/SFX scope remains separate.
  - `MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4` — *Colour card faces by synergy type (two-tone bridge
    cards)* — another card-face colouring effort; ensure the owner border does
    not clash with synergy two-tone faces.
  - `MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP` — *Playable AI competitive mode (human vs AI)* — the
    epic that introduced competitive seats.
  - `MS-0MUTU8J9T0034OT7` — *Competitive scoreboard & active-seat HUD* — the
    current seat-label/colour surface.
  - `MS-0MUTU8ICD002I1MK` — *AI seat configuration model* — where per-seat
    config (`controller`/`aiStrategy`/`aiDifficulty`) lives; seat colour is a
    natural sibling field.
- **Potentially related docs:** `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`
  (visual language), `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` (card geometry for
  the border), `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` (AI seats).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Decision (Q1 = A):** this item is the focused "seat identity colour"
  delivery and supersedes `MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K`'s owner-colour scope; its
  phase-alternation/SFX scope stays separate.
- **Decision (Q2 = A):** a fixed colour-blind-safe palette is shuffled per game
  with an injected RNG and persisted in competitive state.
- **Decision (Q3 = A):** owner colour becomes the outer card border and the
  upgrade indicator moves to the existing top-left level badge / corner accent,
  removing the full-card upgrade border.
- **Colour-clash risk:** the owner border may clash with synergy two-tone card
  faces (`MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4`) or the upgrade border. Mitigation: keep the
  owner border on the card frame and verify contrast in a manual pass.
- **Accessibility risk:** colour alone is insufficient; mitigation — always pair
  colour with the seat label text.
- **Test churn:** the scoreboard/HUD and street renderer tests pin current
  hard-coded colours; update them to the seat-colour contract rather than
  deleting them.
- **Scope creep:** do not restyle the whole competitive scene, add SFX, or
  redesign card faces. Record broader polish as separate work items.

## Resolved Decisions (producer)

- **Q1 = A (overlap):** This item is the focused "seat identity colour"
  delivery and references `MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K` as superseded for the
  owner-colour part; phase alternation/SFX stay separate.
- **Q2 = A (palette/assignment):** Fixed colour-blind-safe palette (e.g.
  Okabe–Ito) shuffled per game with an injected RNG, persisted in competitive
  state.
- **Q3 = A (border conflict):** Owner colour becomes the outer card border; the
  upgrade indicator moves to the top-left level badge / corner accent, removing
  the full-card upgrade border.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q1 — Overlap with `MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K`.** Answer (producer, interactive
  reply, 2026-10-09): **option A** — this item is the focused seat-identity
  colour delivery; `MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K` is superseded for the owner-colour
  part and its phase-alternation/SFX scope stays separate. Context:
  `MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K` scoped owner-coloured street rendering but was deferred
  on 2026-10-03 and closed `done` with no implementation.
  **Recommended:** A — agreed.
- **Q2 — Colour-blind-friendly palette and assignment.** Answer (producer,
  interactive reply, 2026-10-09): **option A** — a fixed colour-blind-safe
  palette (e.g. Okabe–Ito) shuffled per game with an injected RNG, persisted in
  competitive state. **Recommended:** A — agreed.
- **Q3 — Card border vs upgrade border.** Answer (producer, interactive reply,
  2026-10-09): **option A** — owner colour becomes the outer card border and
  the upgrade indicator moves to the existing top-left level badge / corner
  accent, removing the full-card upgrade border. **Recommended:** A — agreed.
- Questions were first recorded as work-item comments and the item flagged for
  producer review; the producer then answered all three (A/A/A) and this brief
  was finalised.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E** – Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card (1024×1024 source; eliminate generic Fallback art) (open)
- **MS-0MUVQRCAO0041SGG** – Human-collapse loss + single-player regression (completed)
- **MS-0MTIIL1ON006H7IL** – Shared-day phase machine: alternating MarketPhases, shared closing phases (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 88bbff, accept, acceptance, accessibility, acted (+299 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, accessibility, acted, acting (+241 more)
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: 88bbff, accept, acceptance, accessibility, action (+209 more)

# Remote hosting of card packs (remote bundle source)

**Related:** `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` (Make card packs available in the browser
distribution — introduces the pack-source registry this builds on)
**Related:** `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` (Make card-pack assets self-contained)

## Summary

Card packs are currently discovered from a single source: a content directory
(the Electron launcher) or, once `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` lands, a bundled
build-time registry. This item adds a **remote pack source** so a pack catalogue
can be hosted at a URL and fetched at runtime — enabling packs to be published
or updated without rebuilding or re-releasing the game.

This is the future-work half of the source-registry design: the registry seam
(`PackSource[]`) is introduced by `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`, and this item
implements the remote provider on top of it.

## Goal (user story)

> As a distribution operator, I want to host a card pack (and its catalogue) at
> a URL, so I can publish or update packs for an installed game without
> rebuilding the launcher or the web build.

> As a player, I want a remote pack to appear in the Card Packs panel and
> behave exactly like a bundled or content-directory pack (lock → purchase →
> enable → deal), while the game still boots and plays offline on its bundled
> packs if the remote host is unreachable.

## Scope

1. **Remote source provider.** Implement a `PackSource` that fetches a pack
   manifest from a configured URL (via the loader's existing `fetchManifest` /
   `fetchCsv` transports) and contributes its packs to the merged pool.
2. **Configuration.** Define how remote source URLs are declared — a build-time
   config constant, a launcher-provided setting, or a well-known manifest URL —
   and how multiple remote sources compose with bundled/static ones.
3. **Merge and precedence.** Define ordering and conflict handling when the same
   pack id appears in more than one source (bundled wins? first wins? reject
   duplicates?). The core merge contract already rejects duplicate card ids
   whole; pack-id precedence must be decided explicitly.
4. **Gating.** Remote packs remain content-unlock gated; the unlock target key
   and the scoped simulated-purchase flow apply unchanged. Decide whether remote
   packs may be ungated.
5. **Degradation.** A remote host that is slow, unreachable or serving a
   malformed manifest must degrade to the bundled/static packs with a warning —
   never block boot, never blank the listing. Define a timeout.
6. **Trust and integrity.** Address the supply-chain surface: remote packs
   inject card rows into the pool, and the merge contract validates the header
   and duplicate ids but not malicious content. Define an integrity mechanism
   (signing, checksum pinning, allow-listed host/ids) and what the game does
   when verification fails.
7. **Caching / offline.** Decide whether remote packs are cached (for example in
   `localStorage` / Cache Storage) so a previously fetched pack remains usable
   offline, and how cache invalidation/versioning works.
8. **Docs and tests.** Cover remote discovery, degradation, gating and
   integrity with tests, and document the remote-hosting contract.

## Acceptance criteria (to be confirmed at intake)

1. A pack catalogue hosted at a configured URL is discovered at runtime and its
   packs appear in the Card Packs panel.
2. Remote packs behave identically to bundled packs across lock → purchase →
   enable → deal, and save/load.
3. With the remote host unreachable/slow, the game boots on bundled packs and
   warns; the listing is never empty when a bundled pack exists.
4. A malformed remote manifest or a pack with a bad header/duplicate id is
   rejected whole with a warning, without affecting other sources.
5. Pack-id precedence across sources is deterministic and documented.
6. The integrity mechanism rejects a tampered/unverified remote pack and
   documents the failure mode.
7. Remote pack art resolves and renders (coordinated with
   `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0`).
8. Documentation covers configuration, the hosting contract, integrity and
   degradation.
9. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Out of scope

- A pack storefront, purchase/checkout, or pack-authoring UI.
- A pack CDN/build-publish pipeline (a natural follow-up).
- Real money/Steam storefront transactions.
- Changing the bundled or content-directory sources.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — supply chain.** Remote content is untrusted; without integrity
  checks a hostile pack could inject arbitrary card data. Mitigation: signing /
  checksum pinning / host allow-list, with a safe refusal mode.
- **Risk — boot latency.** A remote fetch on the boot path could stall the game.
  Mitigation: bounded timeout, non-blocking discovery, bundled-first.
- **Risk — offline regression.** A user who once fetched a remote pack may lose
  it offline. Mitigation: explicit caching decision.
- **Assumption — registry seam exists.** `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` provides the
  `PackSource` abstraction; this item adds a provider rather than re-architecting.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — remote source registration and merge ordering.
- `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` — URL contentDir / transport use.
- `core/src/core-engine/CardPackManifest.ts` — manifest parse (shared).
- `vite.config.ts` / config — remote source URL declaration.
- `tests/main-street/` — remote discovery, degradation, integrity tests.
- `README.md`, `packs/README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md` — remote-hosting contract.

## Description

Wire the challenge evaluation path to pass seat context through both the per-action and EndCheck closing evaluation paths. Ensure consistency across all evaluation entry points.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Per-action evaluation (`evaluateChallengesAfterAction`) passes the acting seat's ID in competitive mode.
2. EndCheck closing-phase evaluation (`evaluateChallenges` called from `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`) passes the active player's seat ID.
3. `executeCompetitiveTurn` correctly carries seat context through all mid-turn challenge completions.

# Render the static shader accent

**Parent:** MS-0MUWNTQ5L0075Y38 — Create a card shader
**Slice:** 2 of 4 (rendering layer, test-first)
**Depends on:** Pure upgrade shader-effect spec (slice 1)

## Summary

Render the `shaderEffect` produced by slice 1 through the existing overlay
pipeline. `applyUpgradeOverlays()` draws the effect as a Canvas-safe Phaser
`Graphics`/rectangle accent confined to the top-left upgrade-accent region
(the static / reduced-motion form). Base cards render exactly as today, there
is **no** change to the `Phaser.CANVAS` render type, and the effect coexists
with the owner-coloured outer border without recreating a full-card stroke.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `applyUpgradeOverlays()` renders the `shaderEffect` on upgraded business and community-space cards and renders nothing additional for base cards.
- The static accent is confined to the upgrade accent region (top-left accent / inner glow) and never forms a full-card stroke, so it coexists with the owner-coloured outer card border.
- Upgrade state remains conveyed by the level badge and the accent shape, so colour is never the sole carrier of meaning (accessibility).
- Rendering uses the existing overlay pipeline only: no renderer-type change, no `main.ts` change, and no new texture-cache keys per level.
- A browser integration test asserts the effect object is attached to an upgraded card and absent on a base card.
- The 64x64 left-art zone and right-hand text column layout are preserved; the level badge and stat overlays remain readable and un-occluded.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `applyUpgradeOverlays()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`), when `spec.shaderEffect` is present, create a Phaser `Graphics` (or rectangle) child of the card container drawing the gradient accent in its static form, named for test discovery (e.g. `ms-upgrade-shader`).
- Keep the draw region inside the accent bounds used by `levelAccent`; draw before the level badge so the badge text stays on top.
- Guard on `spec.shaderEffect === null` so base cards are untouched.
- Add the browser integration test (`tests/main-street/*.browser.test.ts`) asserting presence on an upgraded card and absence on a base card via the named game object.

## Deliverables

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — static effect rendering in `applyUpgradeOverlays()` with cleanup-safe creation.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts` — only if a new helper method is needed (prefer none).
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-shader-effect.browser.test.ts` — presence/absence browser integration test.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — render the static shader accent in `applyUpgradeOverlays()`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts` — renderer interface (extend only if required).
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-shader-effect.browser.test.ts` — browser integration assertions.

# Animate the accent with reduced-motion and replay fallback

**Parent:** MS-0MUWNTQ5L0075Y38 — Create a card shader
**Slice:** 3 of 4 (motion layer, test-first)
**Depends on:** Render the static shader accent (slice 2)

## Summary

Animate the shader-style upgrade accent (gradient shimmer sweep) with a Phaser
tween when motion is allowed, and render the static form otherwise. Animation is
gated by `!settingsPanel.reducedMotion && !scene.replayMode`; tweens are cleaned
up on refresh/destroy; the effect is presentation-only and deterministic (no
RNG), following the existing `animateLevelUp` precedent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When `settingsPanel.reducedMotion` is `false` and the scene is not in replay/headless mode, the upgrade accent animates via a Phaser tween (gradient/shimmer on the corner accent).
- When `settingsPanel.reducedMotion` is `true` the effect renders in its static form and no tween is created.
- No animation is created in replay/headless mode (`scene.replayMode`), so transcripts, replays, and headless CI output are unchanged.
- Tweens and effect game objects are cleaned up when the card container is refreshed or destroyed; no tween/object leak and no measurable regression to the existing suite.
- Unit and/or browser tests verify the animated-vs-static gating (reduced motion on/off) and that the effect never mutates game state, transcript, or replay output.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `applyUpgradeOverlays()`, read `renderer.scene.settingsPanel?.reducedMotion === true` and `renderer.scene.replayMode`; create the tween only when both allow motion.
- Animate a deterministic shimmer (fixed from/to values, no RNG) on the effect graphics; keep the static fill as the reduced-motion/replay form.
- Register the tween/object for cleanup so refreshes do not accumulate tweens; destroy on container removal.
- Extend the slice-2 browser test with reduced-motion on/off cases and add unit coverage for the motion-gating predicate in the pure spec.

## Deliverables

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — animated effect + reduced-motion/replay gating + tween lifecycle cleanup.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-shader-effect.browser.test.ts` — animated vs static and reduced-motion assertions.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts` — motion-gating spec assertions.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — animation gating and tween lifecycle in `applyUpgradeOverlays()`.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-shader-effect.browser.test.ts` — reduced-motion/replay browser assertions.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts` — pure-spec motion-gating tests.
